central_claim: The document's inferential statements are the ones its statistics license, at the n, the family size, the threshold and the uncertainty the surrounding sentence states.

blockers.summary: §5's one PASSING test carries a target-specificity inference the data contradict, and the drug that contradicts it is the one drug of seven that the document never names. The claim is: 'two independent instruments — a genetic knockout and a chemical inhibitor, on the same target, in the same lines — agree about which lines care. It says the drug acts on the target it is named for.' The specificity shown for it is 'non-DDR control drugs at rho ~ +0.014 and PARP inhibitors at -0.010'. But GDSC2 8.5 was pulled for SEVEN drugs, and the seventh — mk-1775 / adavosertib, a WEE1 inhibitor, a DIFFERENT target — correlates with the same ATR+ATRIP+CHEK1 CRISPR dependency score at rho +0.157 (t 3.893, n 601). That sits INSIDE the range of the two ATR inhibitors themselves (+0.173 berzosertib, +0.252 ceralasertib) and is 11x the non-DDR control. The dependency score therefore does not distinguish the named target from a neighbouring one, and 'the drug acts on the target it is named for' is not what these numbers say — what they say is that the score tracks sensitivity to replication-stress-pathway inhibitors as a class. The omission is structural, not editorial: `non_ddr_controls = ('paclitaxel','bortezomib','doxorubicin')` and `parp = ('olaparib','talazoparib')` are the only groups the module forms, so mk-1775 falls into no specificity group, appears in no aggregate, and is absent from the manuscript's every mention of the drug panel. This is a single value reported out of a computed family of 70 (10 predictors x 7 drugs) with the most awkward member of the family unreported. ⭑ The TEST outcome is untouched — bar 3 is specificity against NON-DDR drugs and a WEE1 inhibitor is legitimately outside it — so the pass stands; what fails is the sentence drawn from it. Fix is one clause and one number: report the seven-drug panel, give mk-1775's +0.157, and replace 'the drug acts on the target it is named for' with what is supported — the dependency score tracks ATR-inhibitor sensitivity most strongly but is not specific to ATR, correlating with a WEE1 inhibitor at nearly the same strength.

blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing in the repository binds it: no module under research/manuscripts/tests/ reads this manuscript, and research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json carries no entry for it, so the +0.014 and -0.010 in §5 are unbound prose. A GDSC refresh, or adding doxorubicin (already named in non_ddr_controls but absent from GDSC2 8.5, so the 'non-DDR control' mean is two drugs rather than three), would move both figures with nothing going red.

p1s.summary: §3.4's load-bearing sentence — '⛔ Three DDR concepts clear the raw threshold and none survives the proliferation adjustment' — is true only against a cut the document never prints, and the column that carries the conclusion is the one column stripped of its uncertainty. The cut is |delta| > 0.2 in within-sample SD units (`ddr_up_adj = [c for c in tested if adj[...] > 0.2]` in derive_part_b); it appears nowhere in the manuscript, which says only 'the raw threshold'. The raw column prints a t beside every delta, which invites a significance reading; the adjusted column prints deltas alone — and the adjusted t values, which exist in the artifact, are the ones that complicate the sentence. Recomputed from the per-sample rows on GSE4303/GPL3290 (n_EMC 10, n_comparator 6): S-phase/E2F adjusted delta +0.128, t 3.60, 95% CI [+0.053, +0.203]; DNA-damage checkpoint +0.074, t 2.38, CI [+0.009, +0.138]. Both intervals exclude zero. 'None survives' is a statement about a 0.2 cut, not about the data being consistent with no difference. ⭑ I considered this a blocker and it is not one, because the two that survive are the two proliferation-flavoured sets, while the mechanism's own concepts do fall to nothing — ATM signalling adjusted -0.070 (t -1.57, CI [-0.164, +0.023]), replication stress -0.027 (t -0.56), stalled fork -0.038 (t -0.77) — so the WEAK tier and §6.1's predicate stand. Fix: print the 0.2 cut, print the adjusted t column, and write 'no DDR concept clears the elevation threshold after adjustment; S-phase/E2F and the G2-M checkpoint remain above zero (t 3.60, 2.38) and are the two sets a growth-rate reading predicts would'.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py::derive_part_b, `> 0.2` in the four ddr_up/ctrl_up/prolif_up comprehensions; research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_b_emc_tumour_signature.pooled_proliferation_adjusted_contrast carries mean_t for every concept (S_phase_E2F 3.602, DNA_damage_checkpoint 2.378, ATM_signalling_DSB_repair -1.574, ATR_CHK1_activity 1.06, replication_stress -0.562, stalled_fork_response -0.769) and the manuscript prints none of them; CIs recomputed by Welch with Satterthwaite df from #per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'].proliferation_adjusted_scores against .sample_annotations_verbatim
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing guards it. Note also that the 0.2 cut is NOT post-hoc — `git log -S'> 0.2'` on the module returns exactly one commit (32a7b230a, the module's first) and the string has never been modified — so the finding is disclosure, not tuning, and saying so costs the paper nothing.

p1s.summary: The proliferation adjustment that the entire WEAK grading turns on is driven by ONE of its two proliferation control sets, and the manuscript displays only that one. The module subtracts the per-sample MEAN of Myc Targets V1 and Mitotic Spindle. On GSE4303/GPL3290 those two disagree by an order of magnitude — MYC +0.328 (t 4.42), Mitotic Spindle +0.037 (t 1.07) — so of the 0.183 SD units subtracted from every DDR concept, 0.164 is MYC and 0.019 is the spindle. The same split holds on GSE24369 (MYC +0.084, t 3.34; spindle -0.023, t -0.53). The §3.4 table prints 'proliferation — MYC targets +0.328 (4.42)' and omits its co-equal partner entirely, and the GSE24369 paragraph names 'MYC targets +0.084 (t 3.34)' and likewise omits it. A reader cannot see that 'generic proliferation' is, on both series, essentially one gene set, and that the second set chosen to measure the same thing does not move. That matters because the paper's whole conclusion is 'that is the signature of a growth-rate difference' — a growth-rate reading is weaker when half the growth-rate instrument is flat. Fix: print both proliferation rows on both series and say which one carries the adjustment.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'].contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma for proliferation_MYC and proliferation_mitotic, and the same key on 'GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz'; recomputed from the per-sample .scores rows (MYC +0.328 t 4.42 df 11.6; mitotic +0.037 t 1.07 df 13.7 on GPL3290). Arithmetic check of the adjustment: raw ATR-CHK1 0.2451 minus adjusted 0.0622 = 0.1829 = (0.328 + 0.037)/2, confirming the mean-of-two subtraction
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Regenerating part B on either series. Nothing binds either figure.

p1s.summary: The concepts the proliferation adjustment is applied TO are not disjoint from the sets it adjusts BY, and the overlap is never stated — it is not even carried in the published artifact, only in the inputs cache. Measured from research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#gene_sets.concepts[].genes against the union of the two proliferation controls (398 genes): ATR–CHK1 activity shares 9 of its 37 members (24.3%, all 9 with Myc Targets V1); S-phase/E2F 54 of 200 (27.0%); DNA-damage checkpoint 68 of 200 (34.0%). The four unrelated controls share 2.0–6.5%. So the adjustment partly subtracts three of the six tested concepts from themselves, while leaving the control sets untouched — an asymmetry that biases the adjusted DDR deltas toward zero relative to the adjusted control deltas, which is the direction that flatters the paper's 'it does not survive' reading. ⭑ Stated at its true weight: this did NOT produce the null. The concepts with the LOWEST overlap (ATM 3.3%, replication stress 4.2%) are the ones that fall furthest, and the three with the highest overlap keep the largest adjusted residuals — the opposite of what shared-member shrinkage would produce. It is a disclosure and a robustness gap, not a defect in the answer. Fix: record n_overlap per concept-pair in the artifact, state it in §3.2, and report the adjusted deltas once more with shared genes removed from the tested sets.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#gene_sets.concepts[].genes (the only committed copy of the memberships; emc-atr-vulnerability.json#gene_sets_used carries n_genes and the resolved set name but NOT the gene lists, so the overlap is unmeasurable from the published artifact alone); overlaps computed as |set ∩ (proliferation_MYC ∪ proliferation_mitotic)| / |set|
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: An Enrichr refresh that re-resolves any Hallmark term. The manuscript's §3.2 gene-set table names the libraries and sizes and would look unchanged.

p1s.summary: §5 and the HEADLINE both report the mechanism's load-bearing predictor as 'rho = -0.090, the wrong sign' — a mean of two ATR inhibitors that disagree, one of which is indistinguishable from zero. Per drug: ceralasertib/AZD6738 rho -0.0224 (t -0.595, n 704) and berzosertib/VE-822 rho -0.1583 (t -4.100, n 656). The first is a null; the second carries the whole mean. The document prints per-drug rho for the one PASSING predictor (+0.252 and +0.173, with t and n) and prints only the two-drug mean for each FAILING one, so the reader can see the concordance behind the pass and not the discordance behind the fail. 'The wrong sign' is then narrated three times as an affirmative finding about the mechanism's central variable, when the supported statement is narrower and already sufficient: the predictor fails its pre-registered |rho| >= 0.15 bar in both drugs, and its direction is not consistent between them. Same shape, less severe, in the drug-specificity control for that predictor: the '-0.033' it fails against is the mean of bortezomib +0.126 and paclitaxel -0.192, two values of opposite sign. Fix: print the per-drug rho, t and n for all four tested predictors, not only the one that passes.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: A GDSC or DepMap-expression refresh moving either drug. Unbound.

p1s.summary: Not one interval appears anywhere in the document, and its central grading predicate is a null. Every part-B verdict, the §6.1 predicate 'EMC tumours show the ATM-defect/replication-stress signature — no', and every part-D pass/fail is a point estimate compared to a fixed cut; no CI, no SE, no minimum detectable effect, and no statement of what effect size the data could have excluded. I recomputed the intervals and they mostly support the paper — which is the argument for printing them. Two do not, and a reader cannot currently see either: (a) GSE4303 adjusted ATR–CHK1 is +0.062 with 95% CI [-0.061, +0.185], i.e. the 'does not survive' null does not exclude an effect nearly the size of the 0.2 elevation cut itself; (b) on GSE24369, described as landing flat at '|delta| <= 0.045 with |t| <= 0.71', the raw ATR–CHK1 CI is [-0.120, +0.142], S-phase [-0.094, +0.182] and checkpoint [-0.087, +0.176], so that series excludes GSE4303's raw elevations (+0.245 to +0.311) but does not exclude effects of half that size. The concordance claim is therefore right as stated and narrower than 'flat' implies. Fix: add a CI column to the §3.4 tables, or one sentence naming the smallest effect each series could have excluded.

p1s.summary: The part-B t statistics treat samples within a comparator histology as independent replicates of 'comparator sarcoma', so the effective replication behind the generalising claim is 2 tumour types, not 6 samples. GSE4303/GPL3290's comparator arm is 3 DFSP + 3 GIST; GSE24369's is 17 LGFMS + 6 desmoid + 6 fibrosarcoma. The Welch t answers 'is EMC different from these 6 (or 29) samples', but §6.1's predicate and §3.4's 'neither shows a DDR-specific signature in EMC tumours' are claims about EMC versus sarcoma generally, for which the unit of replication is the comparator DISEASE — n = 2 on the verdict-carrying series and n = 3 on the other. The recomputed by-histology split shows the between-histology spread is real and not negligible: for oxphos the EMC-minus-DFSP delta is +0.551 and EMC-minus-GIST +0.218; for MYC targets +0.376 and +0.281. Fix: say that the comparator base is two histologies on GSE4303 and three on GSE24369, and that the concordance across series — which uses non-overlapping comparator sets — is what carries the generalisation, not the within-series t.

p2s.summary: ⛔ THE MISSING-NULL CHECK COMES BACK CLEAN, and it is worth recording as a positive because it is the failure this lens exists for. Every count or enrichment-shaped claim in the document has a computed chance expectation attached: part B carries four unrelated control gene sets scored on the same samples (myogenesis, adipogenesis, oxphos, generic DNA repair) and the paper reads them against the DDR sets; part C carries a near-neutral control (ATM, -0.034, frac dependent 0.007) and a pan-essential control (RPL5, -2.744, frac 1.000), and its bottom-quartile coordination test explicitly refuses the independence null — '⚠ The null there is the comparator's own fraction, not 0.25^3 — ATR, ATRIP and CHEK1 are one signalling module and their gene effects are correlated by construction, so an independence-based expectation would err in the direction that flatters the hypothesis'; part D carries two non-DDR control drugs, two PARP inhibitors and a plain proliferation gene set as a second, harder null; §8.3 measures the EMC-labelled model against 67 samples quantified by the same submitter with the same tool. I found no count reported as an enrichment without a background. The one exception is minor and is not load-bearing: §2's 'of 21 Europe PMC records naming H-EMC-SS, exactly one mentions NR4A3' has no expected rate attached, but it is labelled 'an incidental corroboration' and nothing rests on it.

p2s.summary: The comparator arm of the verdict-carrying series is hybridised against two different reference channels and two different RNA inputs, and the manuscript describes it only as 'the same print run'. On GPL3290 all 10 EMC samples are `CRH-mRNA`, the 3 DFSP are `CRH` mRNA, and the 3 GIST are `UHR` (Universal Human Reference) TOTAL RNA. Every value on a two-colour array is a log-ratio against its reference, and the within-sample standardisation the module applies removes an intensity shift but not a gene-specific reference difference, so group is partly confounded with reference for half the comparator. ⭑ I tested it rather than asserting it, and it does not bite: splitting the contrast by arm gives the same direction and comparable magnitude for every concept (ATR–CHK1 +0.158 vs DFSP and +0.332 vs GIST; S-phase +0.281 / +0.341; checkpoint +0.250 / +0.263; ATM +0.084 / +0.141). Reported so the design fact is on the record and the check is not left for a reader to worry about.

p2s.summary: 'Fixed before the numbers' / 'pre-registered' is asserted four times; for part D the record cannot check it, and for part B it can and does. The module, its four part-D bars (predicted direction, |rho| >= 0.15, non-DDR-drug specificity, proliferation-set specificity) and the first artifact all landed in one commit (32a7b230a), and research/modalities/emc-atri-prereg.md — the document §5 points at for the wet-lab ask — registers no correlation, no rho bar and no drug panel. So for part D the claim is an assertion about authoring order inside a single commit. ⭑ Two checks come back in the paper's favour and are worth printing beside it: (a) the part-B series-choice rule is genuinely prior — `_series_choice_rule` and PART_B_SERIES_SEEDS were introduced at aebeb586b, whose artifact still read verdict SIGNATURE_NOT_READABLE with no readable platform, so the rule that later selected GSE4303 was fixed before either series had scored; and (b) neither `abs(rho) >= 0.15` nor the `> 0.2` elevation cut has been modified since introduction — `git log -S` returns exactly one commit for each — so no post-hoc tuning is evidenced anywhere. Fix: say which bars are demonstrably prior and which are asserted, rather than one word covering both.

p2s.summary: §4's 'fraction dependent' column has an undisclosed cut and, in the sentence that uses it, the wrong denominator. The cut is gene effect < -0.5 (`dependent_threshold: -0.5` in the artifact, printed nowhere in the manuscript). The values 0.992 / 1.000 / 0.726 / 0.007 are `frac_dependent_panel_wide` — computed over the whole DepMap panel — but the sentence reads 'the axis sits at the floor in BOTH groups — mean -1.340 across the sarcoma pool, 99.2-100 % of lines dependent on ATR and CHEK1', attaching a panel-wide fraction to the sarcoma pool it has just named. The artifact carries no sarcoma-scoped fraction, so the sarcoma-pool version of that statistic does not exist. Related and smaller: 'a within-group SD of 0.190' is `axis_sd_sarcoma_pool`, the SD of the pooled FET + comparator sarcoma panel, not a within-group SD; the two are numerically close here only because the group means differ by 0.0065.

p2s.summary: §4's coordination fractions are printed to a precision the counts cannot carry, on a comparison with essentially no power. '1/20 (5.0 %) of FET sarcoma lines against 3/71 (4.2 %)' is one event against three; the difference has a confidence interval spanning most of the unit interval and no test or interval is offered. The paper does not claim a difference and gets the null right (see the clean-null p2 above), so this is precision and power reporting rather than a wrong inference: '5.0 %' and '4.2 %' invite a comparison the data cannot support. Adjacent, same section: the comparator is defined as sarcoma lines DepMap's filtered caller did not call FET-rearranged, and `matched_comparator_subtype_labels` includes 'Ewing Sarcoma' — i.e. lines whose histology all but guarantees a FET fusion the caller missed sit inside the comparator. The artifact states this and its direction ('biases the contrast toward the null. It is the conservative direction'); the manuscript states neither, while §4's conclusion IS a null.

p2s.summary: The family sizes behind the reported statistics are never stated, in either part. Part B computes 12 concepts x {raw, proliferation-adjusted} x {all comparators, FET arm, non-FET arm} on each of two readable platforms, plus a cross-platform pooled read — of order 150 contrasts, from which the §3.4 tables print 9 rows and one paragraph. Part D computes 10 predictors x 7 drugs = 70 Spearman correlations, from which §5 prints 4 rows and two per-drug pairs. No p-value is printed anywhere, so nothing is claimed at a corrected or uncorrected significance level, and the conclusions are cut-based nulls that multiplicity does not threaten — but t values up to 5.92 are printed parenthetically and read as significance to any reviewer, and the size of the family they were drawn from is not on the page. One sentence naming both family sizes would close it. Related: §3.4's table shows 2 of the 4 unrelated control sets (the two that exceed the cut) and 1 of the 2 proliferation sets; myogenesis (+0.146, t 1.70) and generic DNA repair (+0.178, t 3.33) are computed and not shown.

p2s.summary: The held-out FET signature is honest about the circularity it was built to avoid and silent about a second one. §5 says it is 'Built only on lines with no GDSC data (34 FET, 928 non-FET) and scored on the 965 lines that have it — so the correlation is not circular by construction', which is right about LINE-level leakage. It does not say that the 100 up / 100 down genes were selected from a GENE subspace consisting of the study's own gene-set members plus a seeded random background, not from the transcriptome — the artifact records this as a `_caveat` and the manuscript drops it. The direction is conservative (a subspace-limited, uncross-validated 34-vs-928 selection scored on other lines will under-perform, not over-perform, and the observed rho -0.138 is a fail either way), so this is disclosure, not a defect.
p2s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.fet_signature._caveat ('derived from the columns this run actually read (the gene-set members plus a seeded random background sample), NOT from the whole transcriptome — so it is a signature of that subspace and is reported as such') and ._fet_signature_design; manuscript §5 reproduces the design sentence and not the caveat

p2s.summary: Where this document reports a null it almost always guards it correctly, and that is the reason the seat's headline finding is one blocker rather than several. The guards I checked and found sound: §1 and §3.3 keep NOT_ASSESSABLE outside the three graded tiers so an instrument failure cannot be graded as a biological result; §3.4's 'What it is NOT' states that no expression matrix can measure a recruitment-and-phosphorylation event; §4 states 'it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis. A full knockout removes the protein everywhere; a sub-lethal inhibitor does not'; §6.1 states 'The hypothesis is neither supported nor refuted here'; §8.3 states the identity test 'must NOT be read symmetrically' and has 'low sensitivity by construction', naming the index and immediate-early confounds, and says what a positive would have looked like before saying none was found; §2 separates a reading of absence (ACH-001519 IS in the fusion file with two non-NR4A3 calls) from an absent reading (a model missing from the file), and marks the 83rd-percentile NR4A3 as 'weak corroboration only' against a near-zero panel median rather than as high expression. I found no place where a 'no significant difference' is upgraded to 'no difference'.

_verdict_note: 1 blocker, 6 P1s, 8 P2s. The inferential machinery is unusually disciplined for this kind of work: every null in the document is guarded against being read as absence, every enrichment-shaped claim carries a computed background, the coordination test explicitly refuses the independence null that would have flattered the hypothesis, and the part-B series-selection rule is demonstrably prior to the read it selects. Nothing in the paper is statistically tuned — neither threshold has been modified since the day it was written. What fails is REPORTING rather than computation: the two cuts that decide the conclusions (|delta| > 0.2, gene effect < -0.5) are never printed; the uncertainty on the column that carries the part-B conclusion is withheld while the column that does not carry it prints t; per-drug values are shown for the one predictor that passes and hidden behind two-drug means for the three that fail; and one of the seven GDSC drugs — the WEE1 inhibitor, at rho +0.157 against the same dependency score that gives the ATR inhibitors +0.173 and +0.252 — is absent from the paper entirely, which is what makes the blocker a blocker: it is the datum that most challenges the paper's only positive result. Every fix is a number the artifact already holds.
